title: task edit fails on terminal-status records with misleading task_not_found
description: TaskService.editOn (src/application/tasks/tasks.ts:774) looks up the target via findTask(snapshot.tasks, reference) - snapshot.tasks is documented as the active tasks/ location only. TaskService.moveTask (used by complete/archive/demote) instead uses this.taskRecords(snapshot), which is All task records, including retention locations. Once complete() relocates a record to .quest/completed/ (or archive() to archived/), every quest task edit operation against it - check-ac, add-note, final-summary, all of them, not just check-ac - throws RecordValidationError(task_not_found) via findTask, even though the record demonstrably exists on disk and quest task view <id> resolves it fine. Reproduced live on QCLI-218: ticking an AC while In Progress succeeded; completing the task then ticking or add-note on the same id both failed identically with task_not_found. This is why QCLI-217s six acceptance criteria could not be checked at close time despite having evidence for all of them, and is a likely root cause - not certainly the only one - behind the fleet-wide sweep opum-agent ran today that found 31 terminal records fleet-wide with unchecked acceptance criteria: any record where the author ticked boxes after calling task complete instead of before would hit exactly this. Scope is the lookup behavior and the error message, not whether terminal records should be editable at all - that is a separate design question this task does not take a position on.

acceptanceCriteria.text: editOn documented to state which task locations it searches, and whether that is deliberate or a bug

if unintentional: editOn (or the CLI layer above it) searches all locations edit is meant to support, not just the active tasks/ collection, OR the error is changed from task_not_found to a name that says the record exists but is not editable in its current location

the fix or the deliberate-scope decision is validated against the QCLI-218 repro (tick-before-complete succeeds, tick-after-complete on completed/archived should reflect the chosen behavior deliberately rather than by accident)
cross-referenced with QCLI-216 (phantom-AC checkbox integrity) as a related acceptance-criteria-integrity defect

implementationNotes: Independent Orbitfall confirmation from cli-test on 2026-09-04, installed Quest 0.3.2 (macOS ARM64). After CT-2 was completed, quest task view CT-2 --json succeeded and returned status Done, but quest task edit CT-2 --append-final-summary "..." --actor orbitfall-planner --actor-kind delegated-agent --accountable-human jdnewhouse --json returned exit 3 task_not_found. Recovery used demote, ordinary edit and complete, preserving the task data. This corroborates the existing lookup/diagnostic issue; it does not decide whether terminal edits should be allowed. Evidence: ../cli-test/project-artifacts/orbitfall/backlog-summary-addendum.json (error), backlog-retained-view.json (record exists), backlog-reopened-for-addendum.json, backlog-addendum.json and backlog-recompleted.json (recovery), plus commands.jsonl. No duplicate ticket created.

Live self-repro, 2026-09-05: attempted 'quest task edit QCLI-234 --add-note ...' on QCLI-234 (status Done, completed earlier the same session) to record a post-completion finding. Got exit 3, {"error_type":"not_found","message":"task_not_found"} - identical shape to QCLI-218's repro. 'quest task view QCLI-234 --json' resolves fine in the same breath, confirming the record exists and this is the documented findTask-vs-taskRecords location-scope bug, not a fluke. Workaround used: recorded the finding here instead, since QCLI-219 (this task) is still To Do and editable. The finding that couldn't be attached to QCLI-234 directly: PR #269 (dev->main promotion) failed source-gates on 'lockfile had changes, but lockfile is frozen' because bun.lock still pinned the six platform optionalDependencies at 0.3.2 after QCLI-234 bumped package.json to 0.3.3 without regenerating the lockfile - didn't surface on the version-bump PR because @opum-ai/quest-*@0.3.3 didn't exist on the registry yet to reconcile against; became visible once QCLI-234 published it. Fixed with a plain 'bun install --linker=isolated' plus frozen-lockfile and full check re-verification, both green.

Fixed. Root cause confirmed exactly as described: TaskService.editOn looked up its target via findTask(snapshot.tasks, reference) -- active tasks/ location only -- while complete()/archive()/demote() all use the full cross-location taskRecords(snapshot). Once a record relocates to .quest/completed/ or .quest/archive/tasks/, every edit against it (check-ac, add-note, final-summary, all of them) threw task_not_found even though the record demonstrably exists and quest task view resolves it fine. Reproduced live pre-fix against QCLI-217 (a genuinely completed task): task edit exited 3 with task_not_found.

AC1/AC2: documented as unintentional and fixed by searching all locations, not just renaming the error -- the real-world harm (this is why QCLI-217's six ACs couldn't be checked at close time, and a likely cause behind the fleet-wide 31-record sweep opum-agent found) meant a nicer error message alone wouldn't have solved the actual operational problem. editOn now resolves the target via taskRecords(snapshot) (the same cross-location set QCLI-223 already uses for dependency/parent resolution) and remembers its current location. The WRITE side needed the matching fix: the plain repository.write() path always targets the active tasks/ directory regardless of what's asked, so widening only the lookup would have written a stray duplicate into tasks/ while leaving the real completed/archived record untouched. editOn now branches: same-location edits (still in tasks/) use the existing plain write() path unchanged; retained-location edits (completed/archived) use writeLifecycle with a location-preserving single-entry upsert, the same mechanism demote() already uses for its own cross-location move. A genuine status *transition* (--status to a different value) still goes through transitionTask exactly as before and is correctly rejected for a terminal record (e.g. "Illegal task transition: Done -> In Progress.") -- this fix reaches metadata edits only, it does not relax status semantics or make terminal records generally re-openable.

AC3: validated live against the exact QCLI-218/QCLI-217 repro shape -- tick-before-complete already worked and still does; tick/add-note-after-complete now succeeds instead of failing, confirmed manually against the real QCLI-217 record (added a note, verified the file stayed correctly in .quest/completed/ with no stray duplicate in .quest/tasks/, then removed the test note) before writing the regression test.

AC4: cross-referenced -- QCLI-216 was a checkbox-integrity defect from a different root cause (a Backlog.md CLI flag-confusion bug corrupting AC text before migration), not the same bug as this one (a Quest-native location-scoping bug in editOn itself), but both land in the same "acceptance-criteria integrity" family the fleet-wide sweep surfaced.

Not fixed here, deliberately out of scope: task edit-batch (editBatch) has the identical active-tasks-only restriction (workingTasks = [...initial.tasks], same reason) but uses an architecturally different locked-session write mechanism this task didn't ask me to touch. Filing a follow-up.

Tests: CLI-process integration test (test/integration/tasks/cli-semantics.test.ts) covers editing a genuinely completed task and a genuinely archived task, confirms the edit succeeds, confirms the record stays correctly located (task list still shows exactly one T-1, no duplicate), and confirms a real status transition on the terminal record still correctly fails. Full suite 421/421, bun run check green.
finalSummary:
task edit failed with a misleading task_not_found on any completed or archived record, even though the record demonstrably existed (quest task view resolved it fine). Root cause: TaskService.editOn looked up its target in the active tasks/ location only, while complete/archive/demote all use the full cross-location record set. This is why QCLI-217's six acceptance criteria could not be checked at close time, and a likely contributor to the fleet-wide 31-record sweep opum-agent ran.

Fixed by resolving the lookup against the same cross-location set QCLI-223 already established for dependency/parent resolution, and by making the write path location-aware to match: a completed/archived record's edit now writes back to its own retained location via writeLifecycle (the same mechanism demote() uses), instead of the plain write() path that always targets the active tasks/ directory regardless of where the record actually lives -- widening only the lookup without this would have written a stray duplicate into tasks/ while leaving the real record untouched. A genuine status transition on a terminal record is still correctly rejected through the normal lifecycle ladder; only metadata edits (notes, checklists, summaries) reach the record now, so this does not relax status semantics.

Validated against the exact QCLI-217/218 repro shape, live, before writing the regression test. Filed QCLI-243 for task edit-batch, which has the identical restriction in its own separately-implemented locked-session code path -- out of scope here since its write mechanism needs its own design, not a direct port.
